title: Letting the orb and the drone work for you
target: How the orb and the drone in R.E.P.O. behave when you leave them to it, so a tool that works by itself is deployed on purpose.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: An orb or a drone in the crew's inventory

steps.do: Pick the orb's kind before you deploy it, because it comes in two.
steps.because: orbs come in two kinds, a constant one and a pulsing one (ItemOrb, OrbType)

steps.do: Stand where the orb's radius can do something.
steps.because: the orb carries a radius of its own (orbRadius)

steps.do: Let it collect rather than carrying everything yourself.
steps.because: there is a behaviour for a valuable being absorbed, with its own duration and the value it adds (AbsorbingValuable, effectiveDuration, valueToAdd)

steps.do: Expect company, and know what the company is.
steps.because: roaches orbit the orb with their own radius, rotation speed and noise (RoachOrbit)

steps.do: Watch the orb's battery, because it drains at a rate of its own.
steps.because: the orb drains a battery at its own rate (batteryDrainRate, batteryDrainPreset)

steps.do: Deploy the drone knowing it can be pointed at people as well as loot.
steps.because: the drone has separate targeting for valuables, players, enemies and ordinary objects (ItemDrone, targetValuables, targetPlayers, targetEnemies, targetNonValuables)

steps.do: Read the drone's line to see what it is working on.
steps.because: the drone keeps a line between two points with a start point of its own (lineBetweenTwoPoints, lineStartPoint)

steps.do: Recall it rather than leaving it out, because it runs on a battery of its own.
steps.because: the drone carries a battery drain setting and its own retract and end sounds (ItemDroneSounds, batteryDrainPreset, DroneRetract, DroneEnd)

commonMistakes: Deploying an orb without deciding which kind you want.
Leaving an orb running while its battery drains unnoticed.
Pointing a drone at the crew by accident, because players are on the list.
Walking away from a drone and coming back to a dead battery.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
